items.summary: This chunk explains how to index nearest neighbor queries that include a `WHERE` clause. It recommends creating an index on the filter column, noting that Postgres supports B-tree, hash, GiST, SP-GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types, and that multicolumn indexes can cover multiple columns. For low-selectivity filters, exact indexes work well, but approximate indexes like HNSW may perform better, with filtering applied after the index scan. To handle cases where few rows match, you can enable iterative index scans by setting `hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order`. For filtering by a few distinct values, partial indexing is suggested, while partitioning is recommended when filtering by many different values.

Scans can use strict ordering via `SET hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order;` for exact distance order, or relaxed ordering via `SET hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order;` or `SET ivfflat.iterative_scan = relaxed_order;` for better recall. With relaxed ordering, a materialized CTE can restore strict ordering, requiring `+ 0` for Postgres 17+, and distance filters should be placed outside the CTE for best performance.

items.summary: PostgreSQL 18 adds an asynchronous I/O subsystem that lets backends queue multiple read requests for more efficient sequential scans, bitmap heap scans, and vacuums, controlled by the server variables `io_method`, `io_combine_limit`, and `io_max_combine_limit`, while also enabling `effective_io_concurrency` and `maintenance_io_concurrency` values greater than zero on systems without `fadvise()` support and exposing file handles through the new system view `pg_aios`. It also improves locking performance for queries accessing many relations, enhances hash joins and `GROUP BY` performance and reduces their memory usage, allows normal vacuums to freeze all-visible pages to reduce later full-relation freezing overhead via the `vacuum_max_eager_freeze_failure_rate` setting, and adds the `vacuum_truncate` server variable to control file truncation during `VACUUM`. Finally, the default values for `effective_io_concurrency` and `maintenance_io_concurrency` are increased to 16.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.summary: PostgreSQL 18 adds the `casefold()` function for more sophisticated case-insensitive matching that handles characters with multiple upper or lower case equivalents and conversions that change character counts. It also allows `MIN()`/`MAX()` aggregates on arrays and composite types, adds a `WEEK` option to `EXTRACT()` with improved negative value output for `EXTRACT(QUARTER ...)`, and adds roman numeral support to `to_number()` via the `RN` pattern. Additionally, it introduces the temporally sortable `uuidv7()` function with a `uuidv4()` alias, adds `crc32()` and `crc32c()` for CRC computation, adds `gamma()` and `lgamma()` math functions, allows `=>` syntax for named cursor arguments in PL/pgSQL, and permits named arguments for various `regexp_*()` functions.
items.label: SUPPORTED_WITH_OMISSION

items.summary: The `$effect` automatically tracks reactive values (`$state`, `$derived`, `$props`) that are synchronously read inside its function body and schedules a re-run when they change. Values read asynchronously—after an `await` or inside a `setTimeout`—are not tracked, and `$state`/`$derived` used directly inside the `$effect` are not treated as dependencies. The effect runs after the DOM is updated, does not run during server-side rendering, and any returned cleanup function is called before the effect re-runs or when the component unmounts.

items.summary: In SvelteKit, layout `load` functions can provide data to child pages, which is accessible via the `data` prop in the page component. When multiple `load` functions return data with the same key, the last one wins, so a layout `load` returning `{ a: 1, b: 2 }` combined with a page `load` returning `{ b: 3, c: 4 }` results in `{ a: 1, b: 3, c: 4 }`.

items.summary: SvelteKit reuses existing layout and page components when navigating between routes, so the `data` prop updates rather than the components being recreated. Because the code doesn't rerun, lifecycle methods like `onMount` and `onDestroy` won't rerun and values like `estimatedReadingTime` won't be recalculated. To fix this, you need to make the value reactive using `$derived`.

items.summary: In SvelteKit, component and page state is preserved across navigation, so you can keep values reactive using `$derived` and reuse components to maintain state like sidebar scroll position. If your code in `onMount` or `onDestroy` needs to run again after navigation, use `afterNavigate` and `beforeNavigate` respectively. To completely destroy and remount a component on navigation, wrap it in a `{#key page.url.pathname}` block.
